data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test's failure is indistinguishable from the subject's failure; in shown-to-fail-first installation, the 1/9 mutations lost are exactly those where the guard's failure and the mutation's failure are the same event, so the test constrains by collapsing the distinction between tester and tested.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the guard's failure and the mutation's failure can be distinguished by an external observer, the test describes rather than constrains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 loss rate is independent of whether the mutation causes the guard's test to fail, the collapse is not the mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the installation continues after the guard's test fails, the test cannot constrain by collapse.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a mutation causes the guard's own test to fail, the installation stops and the mutation is lost. The test constrains the subject because the subject's failure is the test's failure \u2014 there is no independent description possible when the observer is part of the observed system.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
